Title: The Habit That's Quietly Putting Your Nose at Risk

Description:
Nose picking irritates and can break the skin just inside your nostril, which can trigger nasal vestibulitis — a red, swollen, tender infection near the nostril opening. A large-scale nasal microbiome study from the Wellcome Sanger Institute, University of Cambridge, and Imperial College London confirmed about 30% of people carry Staphylococcus aureus in their nose with no symptoms — until it gets into a wound.

The urge usually comes from dryness: when the nasal lining dries out, mucus hardens and that crusty feeling makes you want to dig it out. A saline spray, keeping indoor humidity between 40-60%, and washing your hands before touching your nose all help break the cycle.

See a doctor if the area stays swollen, red, or painful for more than a couple of days.
